html:
SMTO-MEM-0001 — Memory couldn't accept a value the Agent sent

GUID: 237aa913-8adf-4af2-81e9-5093a1cc207e
Slug: memory-invalid-argument
Domain: MEM · Subsystem: mem

What happened

  • The Agent asked Memory to save, list or search, but one value it sent wasn't usable, such as a version number or how many results to show. Nothing in your memories was changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask the Agent to read the memory it was working with again before changing it. Reading it again gives the Agent the memory's current version number.
  2. If the Agent was listing or searching memories, ask it to try again without choosing how many results to show. Memory lists at most 100 items and searches at most 50 at a time; leaving the count out uses a valid default.
  3. To make the change yourself, open Memory Editor, find the memory and edit it there. Memory Editor fills in the right version number for you.

What success looks like

  • The Agent reports the memory step finished, or Memory Editor shows your change after you select Save.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO, saying which memory step failed. Don't delete memories to work around this; none were changed.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Memory rejected the request as an invalid argument: a revision or page-size value was not a whole number between 1 and the field's maximum (booleans and numeric strings are rejected), or a lesson-publication request had a missing review, malformed lesson list or invalid source references.

What this means

  • Memory argument validation rejects boolean/non-integer values, nonpositive values or values above the field's configured maximum. Memory validation and conditional writes preserve the current stored revision on rejection. This is global Memory, separate from conversation KV; diagnostic rendering does not perform additional storage operations.

Why this can happen

  • Memory argument validation rejects boolean/non-integer values, nonpositive values or values above the field's configured maximum.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the named numeric field and its exact type; do not coerce a boolean into a revision.

How to fix it

  • positive_integer requires expected_revision and limit to be real integers of at least 1 and no more than the field maximum (100 for list, 50 for search); booleans and numeric strings are rejected. For epoch lesson publication, supply a valid review and a lessons list of {key, revision} objects matching the reviewed sources. Correct the call after reading the entry's current revision; the stored data is unchanged by the rejection.
  • Use positive bounded integer revisions and page limits as advertised by the operation schema; booleans are not integers.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended operation passes its bounded integer argument contract.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • Memory validation and conditional writes preserve the current stored revision on rejection. This is global Memory, separate from conversation KV; diagnostic rendering does not perform additional storage operations.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
